sites.evidence_type: N-terminal HA epitope; parallel surface-display screen
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 5037.5 ± 327.4 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface expression quantified by Nano-Glo HiBiT Extracellular Detection System (surface luminescence) and total receptor levels by Lytic Detection System; receptor traffics to the plasma membrane. Signaling function not reported in this clip.
sites.rationale: MC5R is a GPCR with no signal peptide; the topology landmarks place residues 1–37 extracellularly (EC1) and TM1 begins at residue 38, leaving 37 residues of clearance from the prepend site to the TM boundary (well above the ≥3 requirement). The 'HiBiT-MC5R' naming and the use of the extracellular (non-lytic) Nano-Glo detection system together establish that the HiBiT tag is surface-exposed; the only extracellular terminus is the N-terminus, so insert_after_residue=0 is the unique solution. No residue number is stated in the paper, so position_evidence is topology_derived. PMC9583845 reports a 'HiBiT-MC5R' construct (tag-name-first naming convention) expressed in CHO cells; the Nano-Glo HiBiT Extracellular Detection System quantifies HiBiT-tagged MC5R on the cell membrane surface, confirming the tag is extracellularly exposed. MC5R has no signal peptide and its N-terminus (EC1, residues 1–37) is the sole extracellular terminus; the tag must therefore be prepended before residue 1.

sources.claim: Nano-Glo ® HiBiT Extracellular Detection System can quantify HiBiT-tagged MC5R expressed on the cell membrane, while the Lytic Detection System can determine the total HiBiT-tagged MC5R levels in cultured cells.

literature_notes: L3 (PMC9583845) describes the same HiBiT-MC5R construct and transfection protocol as L2 and is subsumed by L2 as the primary clip. L1 (PMC10390531) reports an LgBiT C-terminal fusion on MC5R used for cryo-EM NanoBiT tethering; the C-terminus (residue 325, D) falls in IC4 (298–325), which is intracellular, so this site is recorded in other_positions. No ledger line supports an internal extracellular loop insertion for MC5R.

literature_other_positions.note: LgBiT fused to the C-terminus of full-length MC5R via a 15-aa linker for cryo-EM NanoBiT tethering; residue 325 (D) is in IC4 (298–325), the intracellular C-terminal tail.
